judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant of an "exclusive right to match the material terms and conditions of any bona fide offer" over a period running "from the expiration of the automatic renewal term ... through two years thereafter" leaves open both what a "material term" is and whether the right attaches to offers made during, or only leases commencing in, that window. "Any or all of the period" is a genuinely opaque phrase whose boundary a court would have to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its trigger depends on the length of the "automatic renewal term" in Section I.B, which itself ends on the earlier of two contingencies, and it must be read with the mismatched one-year notice sentence in I.C.2 and the "last automatic renewal term" language in VIII.B. Those cross-references do not sit together cleanly, so the reach of the ROFR is contestable on a whole-instrument reading.
judgments.clause_name: Section I.C.1 — Right of First Refusal

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence — "Such notice must be given one year prior to expiration of the contract" — cannot be squared with the first, which requires notice "at the commencement of any negotiations"; the two timing rules conflict within a single subsection and "the contract" is undefined (this Agreement or the proposed lease). That is both a lexical and a mechanical defect that a court would have to resolve.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against I.C.1's ROFR window and I.C.3's seven-day/thirty-day notice mechanics, the one-year notice requirement creates a further inconsistency about when the University may even begin negotiating. VIII.B and XIII.A also use a one-year notice concept for different events, compounding the confusion.
judgments.clause_name: Section I.C.2 — Notice of Negotiations for Lease Commencing Within Two Years

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Bona fide offer ... acceptable to the University" and "substantially the same material terms and conditions" are elastic standards, and the prohibition on accepting offers whose terms have "the purpose or the effect of preventing" exercise of the ROFR invites dispute over what effect suffices. The provision supplies a mechanism but with several open-textured qualifiers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be harmonised with I.C.2's contradictory one-year notice sentence and with I.C.1's definition of the ROFR period; the seven-day and thirty-day clocks do not obviously mesh with a notice due a year in advance. That interlocking creates real scope for a whole-instrument argument.
judgments.clause_name: Section I.C.3 — Notice of Bona Fide Offer; No Offer Preventing Exercise of ROFR

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals are narrative and the only strong assertion — that ENET "owns and operates the sole wireless cable system" in the market — is factual rather than operative; "excess capacity" is defined by FCC rule context. Little here for a court to construe as a term of obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital conditioning ENET's willingness on "issuance to the University of a license authorizing ... relocat[ion]" sits alongside operative Sections II.D and II.E, which govern what happens if that license is denied, so the recital is at most a mild gloss. No direct contradiction with any operative provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed commencement date and a fixed end date of August 29, 1998 leave nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with I.B's renewal ending ten years from the date hereof and with VIII.B's reference to "the last automatic renewal term," but the initial term itself is unambiguous. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading says "Terms" plural while the text provides for a single "additional term," and the ENET non-renewal proviso is appended at the end of a sentence whose subject is the two alternative end dates, making its placement grammatically awkward. The conditions (renewal application filed; not terminated under Section XI) are otherwise concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: VIII.B and I.C both speak of "the last automatic renewal term" and periods measured from its expiration, implying more than one renewal, which cannot easily be reconciled with the single ten-year renewal here. That is a specific internal tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any material term ... subsequently changed" is the only soft phrase, and it is a standard and workable ROFR concept. The procedure it incorporates is stated by reference to the foregoing subsections.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because it incorporates "the procedures specified in the foregoing subsections," it inherits the timing conflict in I.C.2, though it does not itself create one. Moderate-low relational exposure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three applications are specifically described and separately defined; "such other changes ... as ENET believes necessary" is a subjective standard but expressly committed to ENET's belief. Wording is largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the FCC Applications used throughout II.B–II.E and III.A, and those cross-references line up. No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Quality and reliability at least equal to" and "at least equal to RS 250B" are engineering benchmarks, but "such revisions ... as the University shall reasonably require" imports a reasonableness standard that could be argued over. The termination-and-refund mechanic is stated with reasonable precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The refund of the Commitment Fee here contrasts with II.D.1, where the University retains it, but the triggers differ (failure to agree versus FCC denial), so they are reconcilable. Also consistent with II.F on expenses.
judgments.clause_name: II.A.2. Design of Facilities and Modification Plan

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "at such time as ENET reasonably determines to be provident" is unusual but tied to a reasonableness standard, and the $15,000 fee-sharing mechanic is precise. "ECC Applications" is an obvious typo for "FCC Applications" that does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $15,000 cap on ENET's litigation funding sits beside XIII.N's separate $15,000 cap on negotiation fees and II.F's unqualified allocation of costs to ENET; these are distinct buckets and can be harmonised. Mild tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts," "reasonable requirements of ENET" and "adverse effect" are soft, but the parenthetical list is expressly non-exhaustive ("without limiting the generality"), which defuses an ejusdem generis fight. The cost-approval proviso ("approved by ENET in advance in writing") is oddly one-sided but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates III.E.1 almost verbatim for a different stage (applications versus completed facilities), and both carve out the Hybrid Agreement consistently with XIII.Q. No real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It calls the instrument "this Service Agreement," a naming slip, and cites "Paragraph XII.A" for best efforts when the applicable obligation is in II.B — a cross-reference error. Neither slip changes the substance much, but both are visible defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The University's retention of the Commitment Fee here contrasts with II.A.2's refund obligation on failure to agree; the triggers differ, so the two can be harmonised, but the contrast is noticeable. Otherwise consistent with the Final Order definition in XIII.T.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts to seek an alternative transmission source" and "cannot be utilized" are soft, and the ten-day clock runs from the Final Order even though the alternative-source inquiry may take longer — a timing awkwardness on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with II.E.2's rescission mechanism and with III.A's construction obligations, and the excusal of STL/PTP obligations is echoed there. No direct contradiction.
judgments.clause_name: II.D.2. Denial of STL or PTP Application

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Conditions materially adverse to ENET" is a judgment standard, but it is a common and workable one, and the termination mechanics and ten-day clock are precise. Little else to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels II.E.2 and II.E.3 for the other party and application types without overlap. Consistent with Section XI's termination scheme.
judgments.clause_name: II.E.1. Grant of Modification Application with Conditions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Materially adverse" recurs but the rescission mechanic is clearly stated with defined windows. Wording is workmanlike.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with II.D.2's parallel excusal of STL/PTP obligations and with III.A's construction duties. No inconsistency found.
judgments.clause_name: II.E.2. Grant of STL or PTP Application with Conditions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Materially adverse to the University" and the University's power to "accept or reject such offer at its reasonable discretion" leave the effect of an offered indemnity uncertain — the text does not say whether acceptance nullifies the termination. That gap is a genuine construction point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Compared with II.E.1 and II.E.2, which state expressly what happens after notice, this subsection's silence on the consequence of acceptance is a structural asymmetry. Still reconcilable by implication.
judgments.clause_name: II.E.3. Conditions Adverse to the University

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All reasonable costs and expenses, including legal and engineering" is broad but the "including" is defined by XIII.T as non-limiting, so no ejusdem generis problem; "reasonable" is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.N caps ENET's reimbursement of negotiation legal and engineering fees at $15,000, whereas this clause makes ENET bear all reasonable costs of preparing the Agreement without a cap — a specific tension over the same expense category. That is a plausible conflict a court would have to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As soon as reasonably possible," "state-of-the-art equipment" and "appropriate space" are vague, and the buy-out price "then-current market value of such used equipment" has no valuation mechanism. "Until the date that is ten years from the date hereon" contains a mechanical slip for "hereof."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to XI.A and XI.B(2) termination rights and to the ten-year outer limit in I.B, and those references line up; the Hybrid access obligation matches XIII.Q. No contradiction identified beyond the timing overlap.
judgments.clause_name: III.A. Construction of Modified D Group Station, STL Link and PTP Link

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause directs ENET to reorient antennas at receive sites "listed on Schedule A," but Schedule A is the programming list; Schedule B is the licensed receive sites. That is a plain mechanical cross-reference error affecting the scope of the obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: X.B.5 confirms that Schedule B, not Schedule A, identifies the receive sites, so this provision is at odds with the schedules and with X.B.5 as drafted. The error is curable by construction but is exactly the sort of point parties argue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition ends mid-thought — "begun broadcasting the D Group" (station? channels?) — and "the first date of the calendar month after" completion is workable but the truncation is a visible defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.C fixes the first royalty payment by reference to construction and broadcasting rather than to the defined Start Date, and III.B keys ENET's antenna work to the Start Date; the two triggers are similar but not identical. Mild inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Technically qualified personnel," "continuous feed" and "intentional actions or gross negligence" are all reasonably concrete, and the parenthetical explains the feed obligation. Little ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses "University Capacity," which Section IV defines, and allocates costs consistently with XIII.N. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same soft standards as II.C.1 — "best efforts," "reasonable requirements of ENET," "adverse effect" — with an expressly non-exhaustive list, so the catch-all problem is neutralised. Moderately soft but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It nearly duplicates II.C.1 and is qualified by III.E.3's requirement of ENET consent to relocation; the two directions (University must modify on request; University may not relocate without consent) are complementary rather than contradictory. Also consistent with XIII.Q's Hybrid carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is a long compound condition ("reliable and cost-effective ... with no material degradation in quality") whose satisfaction is genuinely contestable, and it speaks of digital compression "on channel D1" though ENET Capacity is D3 and D4. The reference to D1 is a possible mechanical error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section IV addresses digital implementation only as to D3 and D4 recapture, so this clause's focus on channel D1 does not obviously mesh with the capacity allocation scheme. That mismatch is a specific relational point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Consent ... not unreasonably withheld" is a familiar standard and the prohibition is stated plainly. Little textual uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restrains the University's unilateral action while III.E.1 obliges the University to seek modifications at ENET's request; the two work in the same direction. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Recapture ... simultaneous use" of ENET Capacity is a puzzling concept, and the definition of University Capacity as "all capacity that is not ENET Capacity" sits oddly with a recapture right over ENET Capacity itself. The digital-compression proviso about "the minimum number of video programs" is also indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with III.E.2 (compression on D1), XIII.M (D2 option), and XIII.Q (Hybrid's rights on D2), and the interaction of recapture with ENET's exclusive use is not fully spelled out. Some genuine whole-instrument strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed sum payable on execution; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its disposition on early termination is addressed in II.A.2 (refund less costs) and II.D.1 (retention), which are triggered by different events and are reconcilable. Low risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration is defective — "the greater of: Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) or (ii) Twenty Cents" omits clause (i) — and "each subscriber to ENET's wireless cable service" is not itself defined here. The defect is formal rather than meaning-changing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.B.1 supplies the subscriber-counting method and XIII.M mirrors the formula for channel D2, so the economics are coherent across the instrument. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bulk-billing formula contains a redundant "divided by ... divided by" construction and refers to "said bulk billing" without a noun, but the arithmetic intent is discernible. "Isolated locations in the same facility" is internally odd phrasing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fills out V.B's per-subscriber measure and matches XIII.M's use of the same subscriber concept. Consistent with the rest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — "the first full calendar month after the D Group Station has been constructed and is broadcasting" — is stated clearly enough, and the certificate requirement is specific. Minor OCR damage to the heading only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.C defines a "Start Date" by a similar but not identical test, so which event starts the royalty clock could be argued. That is a modest cross-provision tension.
judgments.clause_name: V.C. Required Certificate and Payment Dates

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retention period (eighteen months), the audit frequency and the notice period are all numerically fixed; "reasonable business hours" is standard. Definite drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An eighteen-month retention period against an audit right exercisable up to ninety days after service ends is workable, and no other clause imposes a longer records obligation. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Lawfully modify, waive, rescind, terminate or cancel" is an enumerated list without a catch-all, and the consequence is stated plainly. Little ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with V.B's per-subscriber royalty (ENET could reduce subscribers and hence royalties) but the $2,500 floor addresses that; no contradiction with V.B or V.D.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Proportionately reduced" is a simple pro-rata rule, though it does not say how the $2,500 minimum prorates. Minor gap only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with V.B's greater-of formula, prorating a monthly minimum is mechanically implementable. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Placing the burden of "federal, state, or local taxes or fees" on the University while calling the Royalty "the gross charge to ENET" is commercially unusual and the scope of "fees" is broad, but the allocation itself is stated unambiguously.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.N requires ENET to reimburse the University's costs of complying with the Agreement, which could be read to swallow taxes the University must pay here; that is a plausible tension. Otherwise consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Of the kinds customarily insured against by firms of established reputations" and "such types and in such amounts as are customarily carried" are market-practice standards with no fixed boundary, followed by an expressly non-exhaustive list. The vagueness is real though conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsections 1 and 2 supply concrete minimums and VI.B supplies the policy form requirements, so the scheme holds together. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All-risk property insurance ... 100% of full replacement value without deduction for depreciation" is a precise insurance specification. Only the OCR-split word mars it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits under VI.A's umbrella and is echoed by VI.B's naming requirements. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dollar limits and coverage categories are specified exactly; the sentence simply lacks a terminal period. Nothing substantive to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with VI.A and VI.B and with the indemnity in IX.A. No conflict.
judgments.clause_name: VI.A.2. Comprehensive General Public Liability Insurance

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As appropriate, designate the University as either the insured party or as an additional insured" leaves the choice unallocated, a small but genuine indeterminacy. The rest of the obligations are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with VI.A's coverage requirements and with III.A's timing of operations. No inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permitted-programming list ends with "or an other programming agreed to by the University" — a garbled catch-all after enumerated specifics — and the same sentence pairs consent "not to be unreasonably withheld" with an "absolute right to deny" obscene material. Both the list scope and the consent standard are contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to Schedule A, which is styled "representative" programming and cites a non-existent "Subparagraph 3 (C)," so the boundary of pre-approved programming is uncertain across the instrument. Also interacts with IV's grant of use "for any legal purpose ... without any restriction on the substance," which pulls the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts," "all necessary steps" and "required or desired" are broad, but the obligations are directional and their sense is clear. Moderate softness only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly carves out VIII.B, which permits non-renewal or surrender of the licence, so the two are harmonised on their face; XII.B repeats the licence-maintenance duty consistently. Low conflict risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permitting the University to surrender or not renew its licence "at anytime within two years after the expiration of the last automatic renewal term" — that is, after the Agreement has ended — is a strange temporal reach, and "the last automatic renewal term" presupposes multiple renewals. Those are real textual puzzles.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: I.B provides for a single renewal ending at most ten years from the date hereof, and VIII.A requires the University to take all necessary steps to renew, so this clause both contradicts VIII.A's default and mismatches I.B's structure. It also overlaps the two-year ROFR window in I.C.1.
judgments.clause_name: VIII.B. Return or Nonrenewal of License

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnity is broad but carefully enumerated, and "any other claimed harm or unlawfulness arising from the transmission of any programming" is a catch-all whose reach beyond libel, slander and infringement could be argued. That is a modest general-vs-specific point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with VII's obscenity restrictions and with VI's insurance requirements, and IX.B mirrors it for the University. No contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A symmetrical, enumerated indemnity with defined triggers; no catch-all beyond the three listed grounds. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with IX.A and IX.C and with XI.C's preservation of damages claims. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Promptly" and "in form and substance satisfactory to the Claiming Party" give the claimant a subjective veto over the indemnitor's acknowledgement, which is a genuine leverage ambiguity. Otherwise the procedure is stepwise and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs both IX.A and IX.B evenly and does not collide with any other provision. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard organisation representation with a forward-looking covenant; entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches X.B.1 for the University and is consistent with X.C's survival provision. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate compliance and no-conflict representation; "all laws, rules and regulations governing its business" is broad but conventional and unqualified by materiality, unlike the University's mirror clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: X.B.2 qualifies the same representation with "in all material respects," an asymmetry that is deliberate rather than contradictory. No genuine conflict.
judgments.clause_name: X.A.2. Compliance with Agreements and Law (ENET)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence authority representation with no elastic terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to X.B.3; nothing else in the contract cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To its best knowledge" and "any valid basis" are standard qualifiers; the representation is otherwise exhaustively drafted. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors X.B.4 and is picked up by X.C's continuing-warranty rule. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable assurance of the funding necessary" is a notably weak and imprecise representation — what counts as reasonable assurance is undefined and could be litigated. That is a nameable vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands against ENET's extensive cost obligations in II.F, III.A, III.D and XIII.N without any financial covenant elsewhere, but no provision contradicts it. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard organisation and eligibility representation, stated as both present fact and continuing covenant; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its eligibility covenant coheres with VIII.A's licence-maintenance duty and with VIII.B's surrender option, which is carved out there rather than here — a small gap but not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Materiality-qualified compliance representation with conventional no-conflict language; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It represents no conflict with "any agreement or commitment to which it is bound," while the recitals and XIII.Q disclose the Hybrid Agreement and subordinate ENET's rights to it — the disclosure resolves the tension rather than creating one, but the interplay is worth noting.
judgments.clause_name: X.B.2. Compliance with Agreements and Law (University)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite sentence on corporate authority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to X.A.3 and unremarkable against the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Knowledge-qualified litigation representation with an added adverse-impact qualifier; conventional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors X.A.4 with a slight asymmetry that is plainly intentional. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short factual representation tied to a specific schedule; "the site and receive antenna" is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.B refers the same subject matter to Schedule A rather than Schedule B, so the two provisions point at different schedules for the receive sites. That is a specific cross-reference inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Might reasonably be deemed to constitute a breach of or lead to a breach" is a loose trigger for the notification duty, but the survival principle itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with X.A and X.B and does not disturb XI's termination triggers or XIII.S's waiver clause. Consistent.
judgments.clause_name: X.C. Survival of Representations and Warranties

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cure structure is confusing: "either (a) ENET has not cured such breach within thirty (30) days ... or (b) (if the breach is other than for the payment of money) ENET has not undertaken material or substantive measures to cure" — read literally, satisfying (a) alone permits termination even where substantive cure measures were undertaken. "Material obligations" and "material or substantive measures" are both undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XI.B(2) states the mirror test in a single sentence with the same "either/or" oddity, and III.A gives the University a $1 equipment purchase right specifically on termination under XI.A, raising the stakes on the trigger. The provisions can be harmonised but the asymmetry is noticeable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same "either ... or" cure ambiguity as XI.A, plus the unqualified right to terminate simply "if ENET ceases to provide wireless cable service" — a self-triggered exit ENET could invoke at will. Those are nameable soft points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That unilateral exit sits against I.B's automatic renewal and III.A's provision keyed to "nonrenewal ... other than the exercise by ENET of its rights under Section XI.B.(2)," which contemplates the termination scheme as the exclusive route out. Some strain but reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, clear preservation of damages remedies for the terminating party; note it says nothing about the non-terminating party, a small asymmetry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with XI.A and XI.B, which say termination is "without further liability," though a reader could argue those phrases and this clause pull against each other. That is a modest tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence's modifiers are tangled — "all necessary or desirable petitions ... subject to the approval of the University, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld ... required to secure FCC approval" — and "necessary or desirable" is open-ended. The second sentence then gives the University an apparently unqualified consent right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: II.A.2 obliges the University to file the FCC Applications within thirty days or negotiate revisions, which is hard to square with the absolute consent right asserted here, and III.E.1 obliges the University to apply at ENET's request. That is a specific conflict over who controls filings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best reasonable efforts" and "reasonable best efforts" are used inconsistently within one paragraph, and "any additional facilities which ENET may desire" within the "Washington/Baltimore area" expands the geography beyond the Washington, DC focus of the rest. Both are nameable soft spots.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Washington/Baltimore reference sits oddly with XI.B(3) and the recitals, which frame ENET's system as serving the Washington, DC metropolitan area, and its cooperation duty overlaps VIII.A. Mild incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall reimburse all reasonable costs and expenses incurred by the University ... incurred by the University" is a duplicated phrase, a mechanical slip that does not alter meaning. Scope is confined to Section XII.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.N imposes a broader reimbursement duty with a $15,000 cap on negotiation fees, and this clause is uncapped for Section XII work; they address different activities but the overlap could be argued. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence — "Subject to the foregoing provisions, the University may assign its authorization to an entity that does not agree to assume all remaining obligations" — contradicts the first sentence's condition that any assignee assume those obligations, and "subject to the foregoing provisions" cannot resolve the clash. That is a visible internal inconsistency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the machinery of VIII.B (one-year notice, ENET-designated assignee) for a different event and adds a $15,000 fee cap absent from VIII.B, so the two assignment regimes are not fully aligned. A court could be asked which governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument bears on execution formalities. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall assist in the development of such program" states an obligation with no content, scope or cost allocation — a genuinely indeterminate duty. "Sufficiently in advance" is similarly open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes University use of the D Group Station for distance learning, which fits the University Capacity concept in Section IV, but no other clause defines the assistance owed. Low conflict risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional merger and written-modification clause; "with respect to the subject matter" is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Hybrid Agreement is a separate contract expressly preserved by XIII.Q and the recitals, so the merger clause does not purport to displace it. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement of executory character with no operative content to interpret.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the instrument contradicts it. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of fires, strikes, embargoes and the like closes with "or other contingencies beyond the reasonable control of the parties," a classic ejusdem generis catch-all whose reach against the enumerated specifics is contestable. "Period of dependency" also appears to be an error for "pendency."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It opens "notwithstanding anything contained in this Agreement to the contrary," so it overrides the deadlines in II.A, III.A and XIII.R's time-of-essence clause; XIII.R's blanket statement pulls the other way. That interplay is a nameable tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts," "reasonably request" and the sweeping promise not to "take any action which would adversely affect the rights granted" are broad but conventional further-assurances language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-adverse-action covenant could be read against VIII.B's express right to surrender or not renew the licence, which plainly affects ENET's rights. That is a modest but real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Naming federal communications law, FCC rules and DC law together is unusual but each source is identified; the ordering of precedence among them is unstated. Minor indeterminacy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with XIII.K's DC forum clause and with XIII.P.1's reformation mechanism for regulatory change. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings clause; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Given the numerous garbled headings in the document, this clause actually reduces relational risk. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An express disclaimer of contra proferentem, plainly stated; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It neutralises the drafter-construction argument that would otherwise attach to one-sided clauses elsewhere, and conflicts with nothing. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "District of Columbia courts" does not distinguish federal from local courts, a small but nameable ambiguity; the submission and waiver language is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with XIII.H's governing law and XIII.L's notice provisions for service. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Delivery methods, addresses and the deemed-receipt rule are all specified; "except as set forth above concerning the payment of Royalties" is a clear carve-out for V.C's first-class mail. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.C's mailing rule is expressly excepted, so the two fit; no other clause prescribes a different notice method. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Exclusive right to lease the capacity of channel D2 for the duration of this Agreement" combined with a twenty-one day exercise window is clear, though "the University's existing lease ... for data services" assumes the Hybrid Agreement is a data lease. The royalty formula repeats V.B's defective enumeration in cleaner form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with XIII.Q, which subordinates ENET's rights to Hybrid's, and with Section IV's definition of ENET Capacity as D3 and D4; adding D2 to ENET Capacity is expressly provided for, so the pieces fit. Mild interplay only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The $15,000 cap is expressed as a parenthetical on "reasonable legal and engineering fees" within the negotiation limb only, leaving it arguable whether the cap reaches the other listed categories. That placement is a genuine scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: II.F allocates all reasonable costs including legal and engineering of preparing this Agreement to ENET without any cap, and XII.C imposes an uncapped reimbursement duty for Section XII work; this clause opens "notwithstanding anything to the contrary," setting up a precedence fight. That is a specific conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Airtime use relationship and not a joint venture" is a standard characterisation clause; the second sentence's prohibition on presenting "as having any relationship with one another" is oddly absolute but qualified by the exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.C requires ENET to list University programming in its program guide, which involves some public association, but the "except as set forth under the terms of this Agreement" carve-out covers it. Low conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Adversely affect the ability of the parties to perform" and an agreement to "negotiate in good faith to reform" leave the outcome indeterminate, and "any action that contributes to such adverse amendment" is a very broad prohibition on regulatory advocacy. Both are nameable soft terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with XIII.P.2's acknowledgement that FCC rules may change the capacity allocation and with VIII.A's compliance duties; the two subsections of P are complementary. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short acknowledgement of regulatory contingency; note the Report and Order release date is given as July 9, 1994 here and July 6, 1994 in Section IV — a factual discrepancy in the citation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The differing release dates for the same FCC order between this clause and Section IV is a small internal inconsistency, though it does not change substance. Otherwise consistent with XIII.P.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall be read to conform to such other obligations that the University may owe to Hybrid" is an open-ended subordination whose reach into ENET's rights is unbounded, and "in the reasonable judgment of the University after consultation with Hybrid" makes the trigger largely the University's call. That is genuinely elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It opens "notwithstanding anything to the contrary" and therefore qualifies III.A's access obligations, IV's capacity grant and XIII.M's D2 option, none of which reference it; whether it can hollow out ENET's core bargain is exactly a whole-instrument question. That is a real relational tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blanket time-of-essence declaration is definite in form, though its application to "reasonable" and "best efforts" deadlines is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.F automatically extends performance periods for force majeure, and III.A uses "as soon as reasonably possible," so a strict time-of-essence rule does not sit perfectly with those provisions. Moderate tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-waiver language; "express or implied waiver" and the past/future formulation are conventional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with XI's cure-and-terminate mechanics and X.C's survival clause. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitions of "including" and "Final Order" are carefully drafted with lettered conditions; "variations therefore" is a typo for "thereof" with no substantive effect. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Final Order definition is invoked throughout II.D, II.E, III.A, VIII.B and XIII.A and works consistently there. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It labels the list "representative types of programming that Eastern intends to transmit" and cites "Subparagraph 3 (C)," which does not exist in this Agreement — a mechanical cross-reference error, and "representative" undercuts any exhaustive reading of the list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII treats the Schedule A networks as a defined set of pre-approved programming requiring University consent for anything else, whereas the schedule presents itself as merely illustrative; that is a direct tension over whether the list is closed.
